Article Title: Tilak Varma in India’s ODI World Cup plans as selectors seek Shreyas Iyer backup
Article Text:
India's Shreyas Iyer, center, with batting partner Tilak Varma (AP/PTI)

Selectors wary of moving batters around

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Team for Afg series likely by Sept 3

New Delhi: India’s team management and selectors are working on backups for the middle order ahead of the ODI World Cup next year. TOI has learnt that Tilak Varma’s name has come up as a potential backup option for Shreyas Iyer in the top six of the batting lineup.Tilak, being a left-handed batter, is seen as someone who can break the monotony of right-handers in the batting lineup. Tilak has been asked to work on his bowling since it is believed that his off-breaks have a lot of potential. The team management, in fact, has flagged the dearth of bowling options in the top order, citing it as a reason for extra pressure on the lower order and the bowlers.The planning for the ODI World Cup will only begin in earnest when India reach New Zealand in October, since most of the first-choice players will not be available for the ODI series against West Indies at home from September 27. A full-strength T20 team is also scheduled to travel to Japan for the Asian Games at the same time.“Head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shubman Gill feel there isn’t any backup ready for the middle order. With Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy being prone to injuries, they want someone in the top order who can at least chip in with four overs in an ODI,” a BCCI source said.Over the last year, the team management has been compelled to play either Washington Sundar or Axar Patel at No.5 or No. 6 to balance the playing XI. In the last series in England, Ishan Kishan was sent in ahead of vice-captain Iyer.“The team has to be prepared for conditions in South Africa in the World Cup. Iyer got injured in Australia and his game against pace and bounce is untested of late. The team already has two ageing players in Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. They are having niggles as well. KL Rahul too will be over 35 by the time the World Cup comes around. Ravindra Jadeja isn’t a certainty either. The fielding of the team has suffered due to fitness issues. The team management feels that they need younger backups ready,” the source said.The selectors, it is learnt, are not comfortable with playing batters out of position. Last year, Ruturaj Gaikwad was played at No. 4 and scored a hundred against South Africa in Raipur. But he has not been picked in the ODI team since.“Gaikwad was picked as backup opener since Gill was injured. The team management feels Tilak could have been tried in that place. That’s why they don’t want to rush Devdutt Padikkal in the ODI setup because he found his calling in white-ball cricket while opening the batting,” the source said.The team for the West Indies series, however, will be an anomaly since Iyer, Tilak, Ishan and Axar will not be available. The selectors are more focused on picking another wicketkeeper for the series.The selection committee is due to meet by September 3 to pick the team for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi from September 13.Sources said that the selectors are likely to retain the team selected for the subsequent Asian Games. The official fitness reports of Hardik, Nitish Reddy and Jasprit Bumrah are awaited. Varun Chakravarthy has regained full fitness, it is learnt.
Article Summary: Tilak Varma’s name has come up as a potential backup option for Shreyas Iyer in the top six of the batting lineup. Tilak has been asked to work on his bowling since it is believed that his off-breaks have a lot of potential. The planning for the ODI World Cup will only begin in earnest when India reach New Zealand.

Article Title: Samay Raina in soup again over remarks on people from Bihar, Kashmiri Pandits: 'They get publicity for free'
Article Text:
Comedian Samay Raina released another episode of India's Got Latent, Season 2, on Friday.

'Cannot be treated as subjects of ridicule'

'Didn't sit well with me either'

Kashmiri Pandit's react to remarks

Poll Vote & Share your view Should comedians avoid making jokes about cultural backgrounds? Yes, it's disrespectful No, it's part of the art of comedy 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

'Absuing is talent?'





MUMBAI: Comedian Samay Raina released another episode of India's Got Latent, Season 2, on Friday, with parts of the show later circulating on social media.The episode has drawn attention over alleged remarks about people from Bihar and Kashmiri Pandits made during an interaction involving Raina and stand-up comedian Sharon Verma.The exchange began when Samay introduced Sharon to the audience in his usual style, making a joke about her Bihar background. He said, “She is from Bihar. She is so Bihari; she thinks ‘ebola’ means someone said something.”Sharon responded with a joke targeting Samay’s Kashmiri roots, telling him, “Samay is so Kashmiri; he loves getting stoned.”Samay continued the banter, adding, “Sharon Verma is a Bihari who came to Mumbai in search of a job. Just Bihari things.”Sharon then said, “At least, I left my state by my choice.” BJP MLA Ram Kadam criticised the alleged remarks and said they were made for publicity."There are certain forces in society that deliberately make controversial statements simply to gain publicity. Their sole objective is to become famous. We need to understand that the deities of Sanatan Hinduism and Kashmiri Pandits cannot be treated as subjects of ridicule.""Someone cannot deliberately do something offensive and then simply apologize afterwards. In the meantime, they get the publicity they wanted across the country for free," he added further again.Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam said comedian Raina’s show should be viewed as a comedy programme and that humour should generally be taken in that spirit.However, Nirupam said he was uncomfortable with remarks related to Bihar and a subsequent comment about Kashmir made by a woman associated with the show.“I know the remark related to Bihar wasn't good, and the way the girl connected to Bihar gave a sharp retort in the context of Kashmir, didn't sit well with me either,” Nirupam said.He said the comment appeared to touch upon the atrocities faced by Kashmiri Pandits and that Raina’s reaction also did not sit well with him.“The atrocities committed against Kashmiri Pandits - she, in some way, commented on those atrocities, and Samay Raina, who is a Kashmiri Pandit, was clapping for it. That didn't sit well with me either,” he said.Reacting to the alleged remarks, a Kashmiri Pandit said, "Look, there is no need to give too much importance to whatever conversation Samay Raina had.""It was a comedy show, and it can be called a comedy show. If I am a Kashmiri Pandit, I have the right to travel anywhere in the world; it is our fundamental right.""Similarly, if someone from Bihar goes to Bombay, it is their fundamental right. They can go anywhere in the country and live anywhere for employment or any other reason.""Now, regarding the conversation they had with each other, when you go to a comedy show, jokes keep happening. One should not take it personally, nor should it be given so much importance as to who said what to whom," he added.Another Kashmiri Pandit said, "There is a comedian named Samay Raina. He is a good man. You have seen him. We respect him and we are proud of him.""Comedians say such things, but there are other things behind them. You talked about migration but migration did not happen. They were forced to migrate.""I said that the way a comedian talks is different. It depends on the way a person thinks and how he takes it," he added.The episode also featured actress and television personality Archana Puran Singh and social media personality Orhan Awatramani, popularly known as Orry, on the panel.During the show, Raina also took a dig at Archana while speaking to a contestant.A contestant named AR Tiwari performed Bhojpuri shayari on the show. When Raina asked him what he did apart from shayari, the contestant said he also danced, vlogged and rapped.Raina then used the mention of vlogging to joke about Archana, who regularly shares family vlogs.He told the contestant, "Did you say vlog? Vlogging doesn't need talent".Archana was quick to respond.Giving Raina a sharp comeback, she said, "gaaliyan dena talent hai? (abusing is talent)."Her response was met with cheers from the audience, while Raina did not immediately have a comeback.The latest episode comes amid renewed attention on India's Got Latent, with clips from the show frequently being shared and discussed on social media.
Article Summary: Comedian Samay Raina released another episode of India's Got Latent, Season 2, on Friday. The episode has drawn attention over alleged remarks about people from Bihar and Kashmiri Pandits made during an interaction involving Raina and stand-up comedian Sharon Verma.

Article Title: From 'khana bana leti ho' to 'will our lives fit together?' How India's marriage biodata is evolving
Article Text:
(AI image)

The old marriage checklist

khana bana leti ho?

What’s changed, and what hasn’t

From 'fitting in' to 'fitting together'

The other side

Biodata vs person

The old checklist is evolving … slowly

New words, old biases

The big picture

Every year, India witnesses a familiar wave - the marriage season. Wedding halls fill up, families revive old contacts, matrimonial apps see a surge, and somewhere between the “ladka kya karta hai?” and “ladki ko kya pasand hai?”, the search for a perfect match begins.India records approximately 10 million marriages a year, or roughly 30,000 weddings a day, according to BiodataPlus.in.Amid the rituals, celebrations and matchmaking conversations comes a quieter ritual: the biodata.What looks like a simple one-page profile is, in fact, a snapshot of a changing India, reflecting what families still look for, what young Indians now expect from a partner and how the idea of a “good match” is being rewritten.For years, a marriage biodata followed an almost predictable template: age, height, complexion, caste, salary and family background.For women, descriptions such as “fair”, “homely” and “well-mannered” were not unusual. For men, a stable job, income, property and family status often carried considerable weight.Recalling her experience, 52-year-old Mamata from Uttar Pradesh, told TOI these factors continue to play a major role in rural areas, although expectations have evolved as one moves towards urban India. “During my time, a few family members used to visit the girl’s family and ask questions about her height, age, hobbies and, most importantly, whether she could cook (). The girl’s family wasn’t really allowed to ask questions to the other side.That used to be a very awkward conversation,” she said.But she sees a clear difference in how the next generation approaches marriage.“My daughter has her own perspective and priorities. If parents of my generation were looking for a match for her, we would consider the factors I mentioned above. But those things may not matter to my daughter because she is working and living abroad,” she said.The difference, then, may not simply be about what appears on a biodata. It is also about who gets to decide what matters.So, has the marriage biodata itself really changed?Not really.Shalini Singh, founder of matchmaking platform Andwemet, believes the format has remained surprisingly similar, even as expectations around marriage have evolved.“Honestly, the biodata format itself hasn't changed much because what needs to change is the mindset of the people creating them. That kind of change is hard, but it's the only way forward. And the people who are willing to evolve their biodata are the ones finding better matches,” she said.Relationship coach Sidhharrth S Kumaar of NumroVani sees the shift less in the document itself and more in its purpose.According to him, the question is gradually moving from “Is this family socially suitable?” to “Can these two individuals realistically build a life together?”He also points to a change in who controls the process. While parents were once the primary custodians of marriage biodatas, individuals are increasingly taking charge of their own profiles and decisions, sometimes with guidance from relationship or matrimonial coaches and even AI.“Parents use the biodata to reduce social uncertainty, while their children use it to reduce relationship uncertainty,” noted Kumaar.That distinction captures one of the biggest changes in the modern marriage search.Verona Matchmaking, another platform TOI spoke to, points to another broader shift: the changing role of courtship itself. Young Indians increasingly want the opportunity to date, spend time together and genuinely get to know each other before deciding to marry. Which was yes- not a case earlier.But there is an interesting contradiction. As people become better at describing exactly what they want in a partner, there is also a risk of becoming too good at filtering people out.Verona Matchmaking therefore emphasises the importance of keeping an open mind during the process. The objective, it suggests, “should not be to find someone who perfectly matches every item on a checklist, but to find someone worth getting to know.”For people currently looking for a partner, the shift is increasingly visible in the questions they ask.Rupali Rani, an account manager at The Reppro who is currently looking for a match, told TOI that financial stability is important but no longer enough. “For me, financial stability is only one part of the picture. I want to know how a person thinks, communicates, treats people and looks at life. I would rather have a good conversation with someone and realise that our values align than tick ten boxes on a biodata and then struggle to have a conversation in real life,” she said.For Rani, the change is particularly visible in what women expect from marriage. “It is now less about ‘Will you fit into my family?’ and more about ‘Will our lives fit together?’” she said.“I would rather have an uncomfortable conversation in the beginning than a comfortable misunderstanding that becomes a problem later. My career, my lifestyle and my independence are important to me. Of course, being in a relationship means making adjustments; both people will have to. But adjustment and compromise are not the same thing,” she added.Data cited by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) also points to broader changes in women’s lives.In India, efforts to delay girls’ marriage have contributed to a decline in marriages before the age of 18, from 47% in 2006 to 23% in 2019-2021. Over the same period, the proportion of girls completing higher secondary education increased from 34% to 48%.But women aren't the only ones rewriting the rules of modern matchmaking. Men, too, are pushing back against transactional evaluations in search of genuine emotional alignment.Shivam Sharma, who is currently looking for a match, told TOI that questions about his CTC, job, property, family responsibilities and career plans are common, particularly from the prospective bride’s family.He understands why families ask such questions but believes a man's worth should not be reduced to his income or assets.“Someone may have a very high salary or own properties worth crores, but that doesn't guarantee that he will be a good husband, that he will bring happiness to his partner, or that the relationship will be free from dishonesty or conflicts,” he said.Instead, Sharma believes families should also ask about a man’s ambitions, values, work ethic, financial plans and how he views his responsibilities towards his family.He also sees a change in who gets the final say.“Both families may still be involved, but ultimately, the decision is increasingly being left to the two people who are actually going to spend their lives together. I think that is an important and positive change,” he said.Traditional expectations from women, however, have not disappeared. Sharma said terms such as “good family” and “homely” can still influence matchmaking, but personally, he does not consider appearance-based factors such as height or fairness important.“For me, good nature, mutual understanding, compatibility and family values matter much more than someone's appearance,” he said.He also does not expect his future wife to give up her ambitions, friendships, interests or individuality after marriage.“If she wants to travel, spend time with her friends, watch a movie, go on a long drive or pursue something that makes her happy, I don't think marriage should stop her from doing those things. She should have her own space and freedom, just as I would expect to have mine,” he said.Major decisions, including family planning, should also be discussed and taken jointly, he added.“Marriage should involve adjustments from both sides, not sacrifices expected from only one person,” Sharma said.For those who have gone through matchmaking, the importance of a biodata can look different in hindsight. What seems important while searching for a partner may not always matter once two people begin building a life together.Vaibhavi Srivastava, an assistant account manager in corporate communications and PR, and Prakhar Mathur, a software test engineer, are now married. Speaking to TOI, they shared what they looked for in each other's biodatas and how their idea of a “good match” has evolved.Srivastava focused more on the individual than the family. She looked for educational qualifications, career, future plans and a progressive, open-minded partner who would support her ambitions. A relatively small family was also a preference.Mathur initially considered age, but soon focused on personality, education and career goals. He liked that Srivastava had “her own goals and clear ideas regarding her future”.For both, compatibility and mutual support mattered more than ticking boxes. Srivastava now places greater emphasis on family values and communication, while Mathur believes biodatas reveal only so much.“Real priorities will come to the fore during a conversation about your way of communication and your view of life,” he said.Neither considered caste or family status deciding factors. Ultimately, they said, the relationship is between the two people getting married.Yet the shift towards compatibility does not mean the traditional marriage checklist has disappeared. Caste, complexion, height, income and family background continue to influence partner selection, though their importance varies across families and generations.Sharma believes caste still matters, but the barrier is thinner than it was for his parents' generation. Greater interaction through education, workplaces and social circles, he said, has made young people more open to cross-caste relationships.“I don't think caste has disappeared, but I do think compatibility, understanding and individual choice are becoming more important,” he said, adding that marriage decisions are increasingly about the two people rather than their caste backgrounds.Rani sees a similar transition. Preferences for someone “fair”, “homely” or from a “good family” remain, she said, even as others prioritise stable careers, emotional maturity and shared values.“We are in a transition phase. The old checklist hasn't disappeared; it has simply started sharing space with a new one,” she said.Ankur Gola, a resident of Delhi, who recently got married, told TOI, “my family was on board with whoever I'm considering but there was an orthodox condition that person should not be of lower cast or muslim; which was difficult for me to accept as they never taught me to discriminate against people... I decided to break the cycle.”Sidhharrth Kumaar takes the argument a step further. He believes traditional factors have not necessarily disappeared, they have sometimes simply been given newer names.Caste, he said, may be described as “cultural compatibility” or “similar traditions”. Complexion and appearance may become “presentable”, “well-groomed” or “fitness-conscious”, while family status may appear as “similar upbringing”, “compatible lifestyle” or “well-settled family”.Even the phrase “our vibes did not match”, he said, can sometimes become a convenient umbrella for discomfort related to appearance, accent, class, caste-coded habits or family culture without explicitly naming the criterion.“These expressions are not inherently discriminatory, but they can camouflage older preferences. The language of matchmaking has modernised faster than the underlying selection criteria,” he said.The transition, therefore, is not a clean break from the past.The vocabulary of matchmaking may be changing, but some of the old filters continue to quietly shape who gets considered a “good match”.The traditional one-page marriage biodata is no longer confined to a printed sheet passed between relatives, family friends or neighbours.Increasingly, matchmaking has moved online, with profiles becoming searchable, editable and instantly shareable.That has changed the reach of the biodata.What once travelled through a limited family or community network can now be shared far beyond it, sometimes with hundreds or thousands of potential matches.Yet technology has not necessarily erased tradition.Instead, the old checklist has found a new home online.A profile can still ask about caste, family, profession and income, even as it increasingly includes interests, lifestyle, career aspirations and expectations from a partner.The format has become digital. The conversation around it is becoming more personal.And perhaps that is the real evolution of the Indian marriage biodata.It is no longer only asking, “Is this person suitable for our family?”Increasingly, the question is becoming:“Can these two people build a life that works for both of them?”The biodata may still fit on one page. But the definition of a “good match” is getting much bigger.
Article Summary: India records approximately 10 million marriages a year, or roughly 30,000 weddings a day, according to BiodataPlus.in. For years, a marriage biodata followed an almost predictable template: age, height, complexion, caste, salary and family background. For women, descriptions such as “fair”, “homely” and “well-mannered” were not unusual. For men, a stable job, income, property and family status often carried considerable weight.

Article Title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
Article Text:
Those in favour of the alliance have drawn strength fromModi’s meeting with Badal, on Aug 7, and the subsequent talks between the two parties

NEW DELHI: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are likely to revive their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly polls, with both parties acknowledging that it could be their best bet despite differences, especially over seat sharing.Since PM Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal on Aug 7, sources said both parties have engaged in talks. BJP will take the final call and has given no public hint about an alliance. Some Punjab functionaries said both parties had shown more pragmatism than in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, when their inflexibility derailed talks. Sources said ironing out the details of the alliance would prove more difficult than reaching an agreement on the alliance itself.Akali Dal is expected to remain the senior partner, but BJP is seeking a major increase in its seat share from the 2017 assembly polls, besides a bigger role in any future govt. BJP's vote share has risen since it began fighting elections alone, helped by the induction of several regional leaders from different parties. It crossed 18.5% in 2024, against nearly 13.5% for SAD.SAD and BJP fought 94 and 23 seats, respectively, when they contested the 2017 polls together. There is wide acknowledgement that the old equation no longer holds after a string of setbacks for SAD. The key question is how the two parties define the new alliance.
Article Summary: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are likely to revive their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly polls. Both parties acknowledge that it could be their best bet despite differences, especially over seat sharing. Since PM Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal on Aug 7, sources said both parties have engaged in talks.

Article Title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
Article Text:
'Unity in diversity in Bharat's DNA: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat

‘Be true to America’: RSS chief message to diaspora

Highlights responsibility towards others

Bhagwat offers interpretation of Dharma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat , addressing around 5,000 members of Indian-American organisations at Madison Square Garden in New York, spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora, while arguing that material success alone cannot define a fulfilling life.Bhagwat was speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration”, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue. He framed his address around the idea of “oneness”, drawing parallels between the pluralism associated with the United States and what he described as Bharat’s “unity in diversity”.“When we say America, United States of America, one word is often discussed frequently. That is pluralism,” Bhagwat said. “And when we say Bharat, another word, another phrase is discussed: unity in diversity.”“For Bharat, this unity and diversity, both are in their DNA,” he said.Bhagwat said differences between people were a natural feature of life, but argued that these differences existed alongside an underlying sense of oneness.“So many styles of living. We appear different. We are different,” he said, pointing to differences in people's everyday needs and circumstances.“But there is innate oneness. That is why we feel for each other,” he added.He described diversity as the “decoration of oneness”, presenting unity not as the absence of differences but as something that exists beneath them.Bhagwat also linked this idea to what he described as the responsibilities of individuals, societies and nations. Nations, he said, should not be seen merely as geographical entities but as having a larger purpose.“These nations are not merely geographical entities. In the design of this universe, nations have to carry out a duty,” he said, quoting Swami Vivekananda's formulation that every nation has a message, a mission and a destiny.Turning to the Indian diaspora in the United States, Bhagwat said Indians living abroad had a primary responsibility towards the country where they lived and worked.“So we are Americans, and we should be true to America,” he said.He described this as a duty towards one's “karma bhumi” — the land where a person lives and works.“The diaspora, Indian diaspora, they have a duty to their karma bhumi. They must fulfill that. They should be loyal to their karma bhumi,” Bhagwat said.At the same time, he said Indians abroad could maintain a connection with Bharat as their “janma bhumi”, or birthplace, and could contribute to the country if they wished to do so after fulfilling their responsibilities to their adopted home.“But it is not obligatory,” he said.Instead, he said, the connection with Bharat should be reflected in the values carried by the diaspora.“Your janma bhumi expects you to live the values it has imparted on you,” Bhagwat said.Bhagwat also questioned the idea that professional success should be measured primarily through earnings and material possessions.“How much we earn is not important. How much we distribute is important,” he said.He asked whether a career could be reduced to money and material happiness, while acknowledging that material aspirations had a legitimate place in Hindu philosophy.“You think of career? Is career only money? Is career only material happiness?” Bhagwat asked.He referred to the four Purusharthas, saying that Artha and Kama represented important material dimensions of life alongside spiritual pursuits.“It is not denied. In four Purusharthas, Artha and Kama are two important Purusharthas related to material life,” he said.Bhagwat also referred to the traditional four stages of life — Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa — arguing that people acquire different responsibilities as they move through life.“So you have to learn, you have to sustain life, and you have to give the advice, your experience to next generation,” he said.He argued that material abundance by itself could not guarantee fulfilment.“So the material happiness is transient, cannot satisfy,” Bhagwat said. “And if abundance of material happiness is there, it may fail also. And therefore there is no satisfaction.”Bhagwat's broader argument centred on the idea that human intelligence carried with it a responsibility towards others.Using the example of a hungry person watching someone eat, he said people instinctively recognise another person's suffering and cannot simply ignore it.“A simple experiment you can do, or I can challenge you to do. When you are taking your lunch or dinner, let a hungry man stand before you, and let him stare at your full platter with hungry eyes,” he said.“You can try; you will not do. Because we are human beings.”He contrasted human beings' ability to think and plan with the instinctive behaviour of animals, but said the ability to think also brought a responsibility to use that capacity correctly.“If you think in the right way, you go nearer to God. If you think in the wrong way, you go nearer to the animal kingdom,” he said.Bhagwat also offered a broader interpretation of “Dharma”, saying it should not be understood simply as religion or worship.“Dharma is not religion. It is not worship. It is beyond all this,” he said.He described Dharma as a sustaining principle that allows people and society to manage competing aspects of life and maintain balance.“It is the balance which sustains everything at once, simultaneously, and simultaneously everyone can progress,” Bhagwat said.He similarly argued that progress should not require either individuals or society to be suppressed.“Individual, society and environment, they have to proceed together, progress together,” he said, adding that different aspects of an individual's own life — body, mind and intellect — also had to advance together.Bhagwat concluded by returning to the idea of responsibility towards both one's place of work and birthplace.He called on people to fulfil their duties towards their “karma bhumi” as well as their “janma bhumi”, saying such an approach could help a world struggling with multiple challenges.“To that destiny and fulfill our duties in our karma bhumi as well as our janma bhumi,” he said.“If we do that, that will be a boon for the world struggling with all these problems and stumbling at every step.”
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora. He was speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration’, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue.

Article Title: Watch: PM Modi takes part in yoga session during Uzbekistan visit
Article Text:
Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan performed a Yoga session in presence of PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in a yoga session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan in Tashkent on Sunday, during his two-day state visit to Uzbekistan.PM Modi walked around the venue and interacted with participants as the group performed yoga. He also posed for a group photograph with the participants at the end of the session.The yoga programme came a day after PM Modi received a warm welcome from Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev following his arrival in Tashkent. The two leaders travelled together from the airport to the presidential palace and later held a dinner meeting. "Landed in Tashkent to a warm welcome by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Grateful to him for the special gesture. This is my fourth visit to Uzbekistan, reflecting the depth and growing momentum of our bilateral relations," said the PM as he landed in Uzbekistan on Saturday.Later, the Prime Minister shared a video message hailing the session saying, "‘Uzbekistan loves yoga."In another social media post he further added, "Uzbekistan was a proud participant in the first ever World Yogasana Championship held in Ahmedabad earlier this year.Some of the medalists were also present today. They came back with great memories of India and the Championship. I commend the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan for their work towards making Yoga popular."The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Mirziyoyev later on Sunday, with discussions expected to focus on trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties.The visit is PM Modi’s fourth to Uzbekistan since becoming prime minister, following trips in 2015, 2016 and 2022. He will travel to Bishkek next to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in a yoga session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan in Tashkent. PM Modi walked around the venue and interacted with participants as the group performed yoga. The yoga programme came a day after PM Modi received a warm welcome from Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

Article Title: No place in Hindu thought for excluding Muslims: Bhagwat in New York
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday placed Hindu inclusiveness and society-led political change at the centre of his closely watched address at Madison Square Garden, saying a Hindu who wanted India without Muslims would “not remain Hindu” and arguing that public opinion—not political power—was the starting point for lasting change.Bhagwat said the RSS wanted to influence policies, prevent conflicts and “stop wars”, but could not begin by seeking political influence. “Politics has now become a game of self-interest,” he said. Change, he argued, must start in society and create a public view that governments cannot disregard. “If there is public opinion, then no politician will dare to go against it,” he said.Speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration” at the Infosys Theatre in Madison Square Garden, Bhagwat said religions were different routes to the same truth. Rituals and religious discipline were necessary, he said, but they should not become more important than the larger goal of reaching the divine.“Diversity is a decoration for our humanity,” he said, adding that it must be “accepted, respected and protected”. While diversity was the rule of nature, unity was the truth behind it, he said.Bhagwat recalled being asked by Muslims during a 2018 lecture series in Delhi whether the RSS’s idea of a Hindu Rashtra meant they would be driven out.“I said, no. That is not Hindu. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu,” he said. Hindu thought, he added, required acceptance that different paths could lead to the same truth and that every human being had equal dignity.He said the RSS had since continued dialogues with Muslims and Christians, even though results had been slow. Dialogue and service, he said, must proceed together. He cited the organisation’s 1.3 lakh service projects and said assistance was provided without religious discrimination.Bhagwat also addressed questions about the RSS’s public image. The organisation, he said, was once “minuscule” and ignored but had acquired “some say” in Indian society over its 100-year journey. He blamed doubts about it on “wrong narratives” and said they would disappear if people saw the organisation from within.Calling for work at the local level, he asked religious and community leaders to create examples of unity and selfless service in their own countries and gradually take the dialogue to provinces, districts and smaller communities. Changing entrenched attitudes would be “laborious, tedious and time-consuming”, he acknowledged, urging participants not to abandon dialogue because it produced no immediate result. “RSS with all its might is always with you,” he said.The address came after days of controversy around the centenary-year event, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and supported by more than 200 Hindu American organisations. New York mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the gathering, describing the RSS’s vision as exclusionary, but acknowledged that the city might not have the authority to cancel a private event.A coalition of civil-rights, interfaith and community groups sought its cancellation, while USCIRF called for Bhagwat’s visa to be revoked and sanctions considered against RSS members. India rejected the commission’s remarks as biased. AHEAD’s X account was briefly suspended and later restored. American singer Mary Millben and BJP spokesperson Nalin Kohli separately criticised Mamdani, arguing that opposing the event contradicted his stated commitment to pluralism.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat said a Hindu who wanted India without Muslims would “not remain Hindu’ He said the RSS wanted to influence policies, prevent conflicts and “stop wars’ But he argued that public opinion, not political power, was the starting point for change.

Sriram Kartik sweeps 10 awards including the ‘Best Junior contestant’ across Carnatic vocal and mrudangam; prizes presented by eminent Vidwan Sikkil Gurucharan on 23 Aug 2026 in MumbaiA fifteen-year-old from Powai has won ten awards at the Music Competition 2026 conducted by Sri Shanmukhananda Bharatiya Sangeetha Vidyalaya and Natya Vidyalaya, competing in both Carnatic vocal and mrudangam.Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of Shanmukhananda's Carnataka Sangeetha Pon Mazhai Thiruvizha, at the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha in Matunga. The prizes were presented by Shanmukha Sangeetha Shiromani Vidwan Shri Sikkil Gurucharan, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, who presided over the ceremony.Vidwan Sikkil C Gurucharan is a leading Indian Carnatic classical vocalist and youth ambassador for the art form. A singer born into a family of flautists, and grandson of Sikkil Kunjumani, the elder of the Sikkil Sisters, he trained under B Krishnamurthy and Vaigal S. Gnanaskandan, himself a disciple of Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and gave his first concert at The Music Academy, Chennai at the age of twelve. Recipient of the Kalaimamani award from the Tamil Nadu government in 2020, Sikkil C Gurucharan has been featured by India Today as one of the 35 Game Changers Under 35 in India.Sriram Kartik won 9 individual prizes — five first prizes, three seconds and one third. He was also awarded a cash prize for being the Best Junior contestant winning the maximum number of prizes in the 10-to-15 years age category.The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla. It drew more than 300 participants from across India and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.Sriram's two mrudangam prizes came in the only two categories open to his age group — a first for tani avartanam in roopakam and misra chapu talams, and a second for adi talam with five jathi mohras, awarded under the TS Nandakumar's Percussive Arts Centre Endowment and the Guru TS Nandakumar Endowment respectively.His seven vocal prizes spanned first places in compositions of the Trinity, varnams, Purandaradasa kritis; the Silver Lamp Prize for keertanams and kritis; second places in Subramania Bharatiyar compositions and Tamizh compositions; and a third in GNB kritis.Every prize at Shanmukhananda is attached to an endowment instituted in the name of an artist, a patron or an institution. He won awards under the following endowments namely - GNB Endowment, the Kalki Memorial, the Dr S Pinakapani Endowment, the BVS Iyengar Memorial and the Lakshmi Gopalakrishna Memorial. The Best Junior award came under the Smt. Parvathy Subramaniam Endowment and S Ramakrishnan Memorial.Sriram began learning the mrudangam at the age of five, under Acharya Ratna Vidwan Mumbai Shri Shankaranarayanan at Powai Fine Arts. A decade on, he has kept at it through the school years in which most students of classical music quietly stop — the age at which coaching classes, board examinations and the ordinary pull of everything else tend to close the practice room door for good.Sustaining it alongside school is the part a prize list does not show. Practice sessions run two and a half to three hours. Nine vocal categories at 5-6 compositions a piece meant something close to 45-50 pieces in which he participated of which he won prizes across seven categories, readied to a standard that would survive a judging panel, with two percussion categories besides.He now receives higher tutelage in mrudangam from Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Academi Awardee Vidwan Dr Umayalpuram K Sivaraman, and trains in Carnatic vocal music under Acharya Ratnakara Vidwan Sherthalai Dr KN Renganatha Sharma and Vidushi Dr Mohana Sharma. He holds a CCRT Scholarship for Mrudangam from the ministry of culture, and presented his mrudangam arangetram in June last year, the day after his fourteenth birthday.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My dad had four jobs at one time just to keep me karting” - How Lewis Hamilton and his father turned second-hand kart, and family sacrifice into F1 immortality
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My dad had four jobs at one time just to keep me karting” - How Lewis Hamilton and his father turned second-hand kart, and family sacrifice into F1 immortality

How did Anthony Hamilton help Lewis Hamilton start his karting career

What did Lewis Hamilton learn from his father about racism and racing

Why did Lewis Hamilton and Anthony Hamilton stop working together

How did Lewis Hamilton’s family sacrifice connect to his seven F1 titles

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lewis Hamilton’s Formula 1 success did not start with fame, money or a big racing team. It began when he was a child in Stevenage, with his father Anthony Hamilton doing whatever he could to keep his son’s karting dream alive. Anthony worked several jobs while also acting as Lewis’s mechanic and helping him travel to races. Hamilton has said his father’s work ethic and advice stayed with him as he moved into Formula 1. Their professional relationship later became difficult, but the two eventually rebuilt their bond. The story behind Hamilton’s rise remains closely tied to the sacrifices his family made.Lewis Hamilton was eight when his father began managing his racing career, and Anthony quickly became much more than a parent watching from the sidelines. He helped prepare the kart, travelled with Lewis and worked to find the money needed to keep him racing.In a 2023 interview discussed by PlanetF1, Hamilton explained just how much his father was doing at the time. “My dad had four jobs at one stage just to keep us go-karting because, when we started karting, the majority of the people were from working-class families,” Hamilton said.That early life was very hands-on. Hamilton also explained that Anthony was his mechanic and that the family travelled together for race weekends.His stepmother, Linda, helped make sure the family had what they needed while they were on the road.Anthony’s role was not simply about finding money. He was also learning how to work on the kart and helping Lewis compete against drivers who had greater access to equipment and mechanics. That experience gave Hamilton an early understanding of how much work went into staying in racing.The sacrifice was especially important because karting can be expensive, and young drivers need regular races and equipment to keep progressing. Anthony did not have the resources of wealthy families in the sport, so the family had to make the opportunity work with what they had.Hamilton also grew up dealing with racism and bullying while competing in motorsport. He has spoken about being the only Black family at some racing events and about being made to feel that he did not belong.His father’s response became one of the most important lessons in Hamilton’s career.In an interview with BBC Sport, Hamilton said: “It’s just how my dad raised me. He said to always do your talking on the track.”The advice was simple: do not waste energy trying to answer people with words. Prove yourself through your driving.Hamilton has described being bullied both at school and on the karting circuit. Instead of allowing those experiences to take him away from racing, he used them as motivation to become better.That mindset followed him into Formula 1. Even after reaching the sport’s biggest stage, Hamilton continued to speak about letting his results answer his critics.His father’s influence was therefore not limited to the practical side of racing. Anthony helped shape the attitude Lewis carried into a career where he would face pressure, criticism and scrutiny at almost every stage.The father-son partnership changed once Lewis reached Formula 1. Anthony managed his son through his early years in the sport, including Hamilton’s breakthrough with McLaren and his first world championship in 2008.But in 2010, Lewis decided that his father should no longer manage his professional career.Hamilton was 25 at the time and said the change was needed so the two could have a healthier relationship away from business. The decision did not mean Anthony stopped being important to him. In fact, Hamilton said he wanted his father to simply be his dad.Autosport reported the management change in 2010 after speaking exclusively with Hamilton. He explained that he wanted someone else to handle the professional side while he and his father could focus on their family relationship.The split was not completely easy. The Guardian reported that the two did not speak for several weeks after the professional separation. Hamilton later acknowledged that their relationship had gone through a difficult period.By 2020, however, Hamilton spoke openly about how they had worked to rebuild their bond. BBC Sport reported that he described their journey as difficult and said they had both wanted their father-son relationship back.That part of the story matters because Anthony’s role in Hamilton’s career was never only about management. For years, he had been his father, mechanic, mentor and guide at the same time.Hamilton’s first Formula 1 world title came in 2008, only a year after he made his F1 debut. Twelve years later, he matched Michael Schumacher’s record of seven world championships by winning the 2020 Turkish Grand Prix.Formula 1 reported that Hamilton became emotional after securing the seventh title, saying the scale of the achievement had caused him to “burst into tears.”The result was the biggest sporting reward yet for a journey that had started with his father working multiple jobs to keep him karting.Hamilton’s rise also carried wider importance. He became the first Black driver to compete in Formula 1 and went on to become one of the sport’s most successful drivers. His early experiences with his father helped shape the way he approached both racing and the barriers around it.The story is not simply about a young driver becoming a champion. It is also about the years of work that came before the trophies, contracts and global attention.Anthony Hamilton helped Lewis reach the starting line when the path ahead was far from certain. Lewis then turned that opportunity into one of the greatest careers Formula 1 has seen. Their journey included success, pressure, a difficult professional split and, eventually, a stronger focus on being father and son.For Hamilton, the lessons from those early karting years never disappeared. His father’s work ethic and one simple instruction - “Do your talking on the track” - became part of the way he approached racing and the challenges that came with it.
Article Summary: Lewis Hamilton’s Formula 1 success did not start with fame, money or a big racing team. It began when he was a child in Stevenage, with his father Anthony Hamilton doing whatever he could to keep his son's karting dream alive. Anthony worked several jobs while also acting as Lewis's mechanic and helping him travel to races. Their professional relationship later became difficult, but the two eventually rebuilt their bond.

Mohammad Amir has ended speculation over a possible return to Pakistan's national team, confirming that his international career is now firmly behind him.The left-arm pacer, who retired from international cricket in December 2024, has obtained British citizenship and a British passport through his wife, Narjis Khan.Amir explained that his new status means he can no longer be treated as a local Pakistani player in competitions such as the County Championship and The Hundred. Players registered as locals in English domestic cricket must declare that they will not represent another country as a local player."I am a British local now. When you play in competitions such as the County Championship and The Hundred as a local player, you have to sign a document stating that you cannot play for another country as a local. So, the Pakistan chapter I had before is now closed," Amir said in an interview with cricket YouTuber Furqan Bhatti.Amir represented Pakistan in 36 Tests, 61 ODIs and 62 T20Is, taking 119, 81 and 71 wickets respectively. He also played in three World Cups, including the 2019 ODI World Cup, where he was Pakistan's leading wicket-taker with 17 wickets.Amir played important roles in Pakistan's 2009 T20 World Cup and 2017 Champions Trophy triumphs.His most memorable performance came in the 2017 Champions Trophy final against India, where he took 3-16 and dismissed Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shikhar Dhawan. Pakistan went on to win by 180 runs.He also impressed at the 2019 World Cup, taking a five-wicket haul against Australia.While his decision may disappoint supporters who hoped to see him return for the 2027 World Cup, Amir's international career already includes several unforgettable performances. His move to British citizenship allows him to extend his career in county and franchise cricket, while his achievements for Pakistan remain a major part of his legacy.

Article Title: ‘The post may end but dream does not’: IAS officer Divya Mittal resigns after 13-year journey
Article Text:
IAS officer Divya Mittal, a 2013-batch officer (File Photo)





LUCKNOW: IAS officer Divya Mittal, a 2013-batch officer, announced her resignation from the service in a social media post about an hour ago, bringing an end to her “unforgettable” 13-year journey.In a deeply personal and poetic note, Mittal said that while her official position had ended, the dream given to her by the country’s soil would remain alive.In a deeply personal and poetic resignation note, Mittal said she had grown up in an ordinary environment with a dream of building a good and successful life. She studied at IIT Delhi and IIM Bangalore before taking up a job in London. However, she wrote that even after achieving “everything”, she felt something was incomplete.“Not being in my own country used to trouble me,” she wrote, adding that her education, confidence and the strength to walk with her head held high anywhere in the world were all debts owed to India. “I had to repay that debt,” she said.Mittal returned to India and joined the IAS, describing it as a privilege that gave her an opportunity to contribute to the country she had dreamt of. Recalling her postings, she wrote that Deoria taught her that standing with the right was not an option but a duty.Mirzapur, she said, taught her that “impossible is not a fact, but merely an opinion”. She also credited the blessings of Maa Vindhyavasini and the trust of the people for teaching her that true strength does not come from a position.Mittal said her biggest realisation was that her personal dreams had already been fulfilled and that she now had to live for the dreams she had seen for her people. She wrote that the true satisfaction of public service came from seeing the happiness of families receiving land rights for the first time, persons with disabilities gaining an opportunity to live with dignity and farmers getting water for their fields.“Behind every govt file is a person,” she wrote, adding that preserving that person’s dignity was the essence of justice.She also acknowledged that she had initially been “foolish” to think she had joined public service to give something to people. In reality, she wrote, she had received far more from them. Their happiness, affection and trust had given her the courage to continue even when she felt tired or broken.Mittal recalled an elderly woman from Lahuriya Deh village in Mirzapur, who touched her head with trembling hands after seeing water reach the village for the first time. The project brought piped tap water to 125 households after a 75-year wait.She also created a free mobile app to help first-generation learners in rural Uttar Pradesh, inspired by her experience of learning French through conversation-based classes at Alliance Française.Transferred from Deoria to Lucknow in May as Special Secretary in the Revenue Department, Mittal is from Delhi. She and her husband, Gagandeep Singh, an ex-bureaucrat, are alumni of IIT Delhi and IIM Bangalore.
Article Summary: Divya Mittal, a 2013-batch officer, announced her resignation from the service in a social media post about an hour ago. In a deeply personal and poetic resignation note, Mittal said she had grown up in an ordinary environment with a dream of building a good and successful life.

We rallied around the deeply human need to be unapologetically yourself — and never imagined how widely that idea would resonate. We are proud of, and grateful for, the hard work, creativity and persistence that have helped build 1587 into a national brand. It represents AAPI history, resilience and a community that has long been overlooked…”The statement continued, "This past week, we took formal legal action against Noble 33 for using our name, causing signification harm to our business. While we are fans of Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes and respect their accomplishments on the field and in the community, it's important to acknowledge that — for years now — 1587 has stood on its own, shaped by intentional effort and cultural storytelling."Things escalated as Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce’s legal team explicitly expressed tht they are just faces of the fine dining restaurant.While the legal battle has been messy, both the Kansas City Chiefs’ star players Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have remained silent about it.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce’s 1587 Prime is all set to extend its hours due to the football season. The Kansas City Chiefs’ star players have been accused of allegedly trying to minimise their role in ownership after being sued.

Article Title: Daejon Love case explained: How a fake 49ers player allegedly fooled 26 women and pulled off a $1,300,000 scam
Article Text:
Image - X

Daejon Love : the man who faked being a 49ers player, bought a $1,160 helmet, and scammed 26 women out of $1.3 million

"That's Google, that's not me."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The internet's reaction has been brutal

Picture this: a match on a dating app with a guy who says he plays wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers. He shows up to the first date in a jersey, a helmet in the back seat of his car, like he just walked off practice. He talks about a future together, about investments that'll make you both rich. You believe him, and why wouldn't you? He even showed you the Google search proving it. Then one day the calls stop, the messages stop, and you're left wondering where your money went.That's the story 26 women say they lived through with Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, except he never played a single down for the 49ers. On August 24, the FBI arrested Love and his 18-year-old accomplice Taylor Jamie Chan at Boise Airport, where he'd reportedly gone to meet new victims.Federal prosecutors say the pair ran a romance-and-investment scam across California, Oregon, Washington, and Idaho for over four years, taking $1.3 million, and the FBI believes many more victims haven't come forward yet.Here's everything that's surfaced since, including the one detail that's making the internet lose it.Love met most victims on dating apps like Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, and Facebook Dating and then built entire fake lives around them.He posed as a 49ers player under aliases including Jon Love, Jordan Love, and Avril Lyto Love, and separately claimed to be a wealthy real estate investor. Chan played the "financial adviser," backing up his fake investment pitches so victims believed their money was actually growing somewhere.Court documents describe just how far Love went to sell it. He allegedly spent over $1,160 on a custom replica helmet from a football gear vendor, filmed himself "signing" a fake 49ers contract while dripping in jewelry, and even showed up to a first date in a jersey with a helmet sitting in his car.When victims got suspicious, prosecutors say he'd send them screenshots of Google's AI Overview falsely listing him as an NFL player, and if they pushed back, his line was reportedly,Once someone ran out of money or asked too many questions, he cut them off and kept whatever they'd sent.Once the case went public, former NFL linebacker Su'a Cravens couldn't hold back, joking that victims should've just tried to FaceTime him on game day. Sports accounts piled on with a running joke that the 49ers' offseason had somehow gotten messier than the season itself between a Brandon Aiyuk contract standoff, owner Jed York's arrest, Kyle Shanahan's car accident, and now a guy who invented an entire fake roster spot.Both Love and Chan are in federal custody in Boise facing wire fraud and conspiracy charges, with an initial court appearance already held. Nothing has been proven in court yet, and both are presumed innocent, but if even a fraction of what prosecutors allege is true, this might be the most elaborate catfish the NFL world has ever indirectly been dragged into.Would a real player really need a Google search to prove it? That's the part nobody on the internet is letting go of.
Article Summary: Daejon Love, 35, is accused of scamming 26 women out of $1.3 million. He posed as a San Francisco 49ers player on dating apps like Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, and Facebook Dating. He allegedly spent over $1,160 on a custom replica helmet from a football gear vendor.

Article Title: New plan to end employment authorization for some spouses of H-1B visa holders: '600,000+ jobs will open up in next 2-4 weeks'
Article Text:
A DHS agenda item says the department wants to eliminate employment authorization for some spouses of H-1B visa holders.

Who are H-4 visa holders?

Are H-1B spouses banned from doing jobs in the US?

What should H-4 visa holders do now? Immigration experts says 'don't panic'

The Department of Homeland Security has come up with a proposal to remove certain H-4 dependent spouses of H-1B visa holders from employment authorization. Not much is known about the proposal and the proposal is listed as a long-term action and not to be published immediately. But it created a major confusion among H-1B visa holders while America First activists celebrated and claimed that if this gets published Monday, over 600,000 jobs will open up in next 2-4 weeks."DHS is proposing to remove from its regulations certain H-4 dependent spouses of H-1B nonimmigrant workers as a class of aliens eligible to request employment authorization under the (c)(26) category. This proposal would reverse the changes made in the 2015 final rule, 'Employment Authorization for Certain H-4 Dependent Spouses,' and restore DHS's long-standing policy of not extending eligibility to request employment authorization to H-4 dependent spouses," the DHS statement read.H-4 visa holders are spouses of H-1Bs in the US. They are authorized to work in the US, and they get an Employment Authorization Document based on a 2015 rule. The proposal plans to remove some H-4 visa holders from the category. It's not known who will be affected if the proposal becomes a rule, but experts believe that those who have been living in the US for a long time, waiting for Green Card may be targeted by the new rule.As this is only a proposal and will take months and years to become approved, H-1B spouses or H-4 visa holders are not banned from jobs in the US.Immigration expert Swatilina Barik said there is no need to panic today, based on the agenda entry, as it is only a statement of intent and not a rule. "Before anything changes, DHS must publish a proposed rule, collect public comments, respond to them, publish a final rule, and set an effective date. That takes many months at minimum, and rules like this are usually challenged in court," Barik said."What is true today: Your work permit is still valid. USCIS is still accepting and deciding I765 applications under current rules. Nothing changed for you this week.""What you can do: Renew early. Automatic extensions ended for several categories in late 2025, so filing on time no longer protects you from a gap. Know your other options before you need them. H1B, O1, national interest waiver, or a permit tied to a pending green card. One conversation with an attorney now saves you a scramble later.""Keep your documents in one place. Priority date, I140 notice, passport, status paperwork," Barik said."Employers, find out how many people on your team rely on this permit. When a proposed rule comes out, employer comments carry real weight," she suggested to employers.
Article Summary: The Department of Homeland Security has come up with a proposal to remove certain H-4 dependent spouses of H-1B visa holders from employment authorization. Not much is known about the proposal and the proposal is listed as a long-term action and not to be published immediately. America First activists celebrated and claimed that if this gets published Monday, over 600,000 jobs will open up.

Article Title: A private landowner has given up development rights on 145 acres beside Zion National Park; the land can no longer become hotels, condos or restaurants and will remain protected
Article Text:
Zion National Park (Representative image)

A once-in-a-lifetime conservation opportunity

Protecting views, watersheds and wildlife corridors

Philanthropy and private partnership make it happen

Part of a broader preservation strategy

What visitors will see, and what they won’t

A model for other gateway communities

Visitors who approach Zion National Park from the east are greeted by a winding, scenic drive that feels worlds away from the crowded gateway towns surrounding many other national parks. That sense of serenity is now locked in place, thanks to a new conservation deal announced this week by the Zion Forever Project. As reported by Utah News Dispatch, the nonprofit has secured a conservation easement protecting 145 acres just outside the park’s East entrance, ensuring the land will never be developed into hotels, condos or restaurants. A private landowner retains title to the property but has handed over development rights to Zion Forever, which will steward the land going forward.Chris Horton, chief operating officer of the Zion Forever Project, described the easement as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for conservation in one of Utah’s most visited natural areas, as per the report. Under the agreement, the private landowner keeps ownership of the 145-acre parcel but permanently gives up the right to develop it. Zion Forever will act as the steward, enforcing the terms of the easement and ensuring the land remains in its natural state.The protected area, a little smaller than one square quarter-mile, sits within a half-mile of the park boundary along the East entrance corridor. Horton said the deal means no hotels, condos or restaurants will ever be built there, although visitors will eventually be able to use a planned, expanded trail network running through the newly protected land.“There are a lot of people that really enjoy that drive in from the east side because it’s so serene and so pristine compared to a lot of other gateway communities surrounding national parks across the country,” Horton told Utah News Dispatch. “People can be very happy to know that that stretch of land is going to look the way it does now forever.”Zion Forever is calling the easement a monumental step, saying it will protect not only the iconic views along the East entrance drive but also the watersheds and wildlife corridors that run alongside the park. The area’s red-rock slopes, desert washes and native vegetation provide critical habitat for species that move between the park and surrounding public lands.By preventing subdivision and commercial development, the easement helps maintain ecological connectivity and reduces pressure on the park’s infrastructure from additional lodging, dining and retail built just outside its boundaries. For a park that saw record visitation in recent years, keeping the immediate gateway landscape undeveloped is seen as a key part of long-term preservation.Horton declined to disclose the exact cost of the easement, but noted that such agreements are not cheap and generally match the price of the land if it were to go on the open market. The deal came together after philanthropist Brian Donnell and the landowner approached Zion Forever about working together to protect the parcel.“Zion belongs to all of us, and preserving it takes people who are willing to think beyond their own lifetime,” Donnell said in a prepared statement issued by the nonprofit. “My hope is that future generations will experience this treasured landscape with the same sense of wonder that we have today.”The arrangement reflects a growing model for conservation around popular public lands: private owners retain title and some uses of their property, while nonprofits or government agencies hold easements that permanently limit development.This is not Zion Forever’s first conservation easement near the park. The group already holds a separate easement for land close to the new site, though not directly adjacent to it, Horton said. In addition, the nonprofit owns six other properties outright along the park’s boundary, which it manages for conservation and, in some cases, limited public access.Together, these holdings form a patchwork of protected buffers that help shield Zion from the kind of intensive commercial development seen in some other gateway communities. By focusing on strategic parcels near key entrances and viewsheds, Zion Forever aims to preserve the character of the park’s surroundings even as visitation continues to grow.For drivers coming into Zion from the east, the practical impact of the easement will be subtle but significant. The red-rock ridges, open slopes and native vegetation that line the road will remain largely unchanged, with no new hotels, condos or restaurants breaking the skyline. Over time, visitors may gain access to new trails that weave through the protected acreage, offering additional ways to experience the landscape without adding buildings or parking lots.What they won’t see is the kind of dense commercial corridor that has developed around some other national parks, where motels, souvenir shops and restaurants crowd the roads leading into the gates. For many park advocates, that restraint is exactly the point: keeping the approach to Zion as much a part of the experience as the canyon itself.The Zion East entrance easement is being watched closely by conservation groups and land-use planners in other park towns. As tourism pressures mount across the West, communities are searching for ways to balance economic benefits with the protection of natural and scenic resources.Zion Forever’s approach, partnering with private landowners and philanthropists to secure permanent development restrictions, offers one path forward. It allows land to remain in private hands while ensuring that key parcels never become sites for large-scale commercial projects. For a park whose identity is tied to its dramatic landscapes and relatively unspoiled setting, that kind of long-term thinking may be as important as any single trail or viewpoint inside the boundary.
Article Summary: Zion Forever Project has secured a conservation easement protecting 145 acres just outside the park’s East entrance. A private landowner retains title to the property but has handed over development rights to Zion Forever. Zion Forever will act as the steward, enforcing the terms of the easement.

Article Title: Players at the US Open in New York are complaining that the smell of marijuana is becoming an unwanted distraction
Article Text:
Players at the US Open in New York say marijuana smoke is becoming an unexpected distraction/ Photo by Dave Dellinger/USTA

Boulter: ‘You don't need distractions’

Jones remembers the smell from last year's US Open

It has been an issue at the US Open before

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 2026 US Open is set to begin on Sunday, but as the world's best players prepare for the year's final Grand Slam, some competitors are dealing with an unexpected distraction around Flushing Meadows: the smell of cannabis drifting in from a nearby park.British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, with Boulter saying it can affect her concentration during practice and matches.The tournament begins on Aug. 30, with Carlos Alcaraz returning to individual competition for the first time since suffering a wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the event with a knee injury, while Novak Djokovic will pursue a record 25th Grand Slam title. Rising star Alex Eala is also expected to receive strong support from New York fans, while Aryna Sabalenka will look to rediscover her best form.Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. However, the venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts.Boulter, Britain's No. 1 and ranked 60th in the world, said she has encountered it both while practising and during matches.“Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot,” Boulter said.“But yeah, I'm not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.“I've played on one before and I did smell it during my match. It's something that I wouldn't like to smell in the middle of my match.“I'm trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don't want to. You don't need distractions. So yeah, I wasn't a huge fan of it.”Boulter is not the only British player to have noticed it. Fran Jones, Britain's No. 3, recalled encountering the smell during her first-round match at last year's tournament and said she initially wondered whether it was simply part of playing so close to the park.“Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round, and I said to the guy, 'is this normal?' Because I was on the stadium, and it's next to the park,” Jones said.“He's like, 'yeah.' and I was like, 'well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well.'“This year I'll be like 'no, lock in, lock in!'”Jones, who qualified for this year's tournament, begins her campaign against Poland's Magda Linette on Monday.Harriet Dart, who also came through qualifying, took a more typically New York approach to the situation.“I mean it's New York. It's New York. I feel like everywhere you walk around, it's everywhere, no? It is what it is. Same for everyone,” Dart said.Dart will face American Peyton Stearns in the first round.The smell of cannabis has become a recurring talking point at Flushing Meadows, with players from outside Britain raising similar concerns in previous editions.In 2022, Australian doubles player Nick Kyrgios complained that a spectator smoking courtside was affecting his asthma, prompting the umpire to ask fans to refrain from smoking.A year later, Greece's Maria Sakkari pointed out the smell to the umpire during a match. She later clarified that it was not an excuse for her defeat.Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have also previously noticed the smell around the tournament.The United States Tennis Association, which organises the US Open, has acknowledged the difficulty of dealing with activity taking place beyond the tournament grounds.“While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this,” the USTA said in a statement.The organisation has said it works with local police and the parks department to address smoking around the boundary of the site.With the 2026 US Open getting under way on Sunday, the cannabis smell is likely to remain a background issue at a tournament already filled with major storylines. Alcaraz will return to action, Sinner will be absent, Djokovic will chase another historic title, Eala will look to make the most of strong local support and Sabalenka will aim to regain her winning form.Boulter will open against American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee, while Jones and Dart begin their campaigns against Linette and Stearns respectively.
Article Summary: Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. The venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts. British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.
